description: Migrate image, audio, video, and binary work content from host-local file paths to canonical url references, with dispatch-time ContentURLMaterializer so API clients can submit file://, http(s)://, and data: URLs without placing bytes on the factory host.

context.customerAsk: Migrate multimedia work content from host-local file paths to canonical url references. Add dispatch-time ContentURLMaterializer so clients can submit file://, https://, http://, and data: URLs without placing files on the factory host. Keep dashboard staging but expose resolvable url in stage responses and canonical content. Block SSRF for remote fetch.
context.problem: File-backed content parts require a host-local file path, which blocks API-only and remote agents from referencing CDN or external assets and ties dashboard uploads to the same host. Codex and providers assume paths already exist; invalid paths fail with opaque errors.
context.solution: Require url on file-backed content parts (deprecate bare file with ingest normalization). Implement pkg/workcontent/materialize for dispatch-time resolution: file:// in place, http(s) download to bounded temp, data: decode to temp, SSRF guard and size limits. Wire Codex codexImageArgs to materializer; persist url in events; update dashboard submit to use url from stage response.

acceptanceCriteria: API consumers can submit multimedia with content[].url (file://, https://, http://, data:) without writing bytes to the factory host except via optional stage API
Legacy file-only parts normalize to url at ingest; validation rejects empty url, unsupported schemes, and url+file conflicts
Dispatch-time materialization supplies Codex -i paths; local file:// uses underlying path without copy; remote/inline use bounded temp with cleanup after dispatch
Remote failures return media url inaccessible before subprocess start; SSRF targets rejected by default
WORK_REQUEST and event history serialize url on content parts, not materialized temp paths
docs/reference/work.md documents URL submit examples and file deprecation for API clients
Typecheck, lint, and tests pass for touched backend, contract, and UI packages
